note: Cross-client composer key contract (UI-quality goal, Phase D). The single source of truth for what each key does in the message composer on each client. Consumed by apps/web/src/ui/ChatView.test.tsx, apps/mission-control/src/renderer/src/routes/chat.helpers.test.ts, and, for the shared decision logic, by the iOS suite. Add a row here BEFORE changing a composer key handler on any client.
why: Shift+Enter inserted a newline on web and Mission Control and was silently impossible on iOS for months: SwiftUI's onSubmit fires on every Return with no modifier awareness, so a hardware keyboard could not type a newline at all. Every test on every client passed. A per-client handler tested only against itself cannot see that. These rows are deliberately allowed to differ per client where the platform demands it, so the fixture documents intended divergence rather than pretending the clients are identical — what it forbids is UNINTENDED divergence.

enterKeySetting.note: Plain Enter is configurable on every client via a shared user setting `returnKeySends` (default false, i.e. Enter inserts a newline). A row whose `enter` map is present is mode-dependent: `enter.newline` is the answer when returnKeySends is false, `enter.send` when true. Every other row keeps the flat `ios`/`web`/`mc` fields because its answer is the same regardless of the setting.

actions.newline: inserts a line break into the draft, does not submit
actions.focus: leaves the key to the platform's focus traversal, does not touch the draft

cases.name: plain Return
cases.note: Configurable since 2026-09-13: plain Enter inserts a newline by default (returnKeySends=false) or sends (returnKeySends=true). Before this the clients hardcoded it out of step (iOS newline, web/mc send) and, on iOS, hardware Enter did nothing because the vertical TextField did not reliably splice a hardware Return. iOS now handles the newline itself; web/mc let the textarea insert it natively.

cases.name: Shift+Return
cases.note: The row that was broken on iOS and correct everywhere else. All three rely on the platform's own newline: the handler's job is to DECLINE the key, which is exactly what iOS's onSubmit could not do.

cases.name: Shift+Tab
cases.note: User-requested override of reverse focus traversal, 2026-09-05.

cases.name: plain Tab
cases.note: Deliberately NOT overridden. Taking both Tab directions would leave keyboard and screen-reader users no way out of the composer.

mechanisms.handler: the client's own key handler prevents the default and splices the newline itself — assertable by inspecting the draft
mechanisms.native: the handler declines the key and the platform's own text input inserts the break — NOT assertable from a synthetic keydown, because DOM test environments do not perform default actions. Tests assert the negative instead: nothing was sent, and the default was not prevented.
mechanisms._note: Present ONLY for clients whose action on that row is `newline` — a mechanism describes how a line break arrives, so it is meaningless where the key sends or moves focus. This was wrong in the first draft (plain Return carried a `mc: handler` while MC sends) and the Mission Control contract test caught it.
